summary:
After the Footprints is an interactive digital archive that explores the human-made objects and spacecraft left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions.

Our project focuses on preserving the history of these forgotten artifacts by bringing their stories, scientific contributions, and mission details together in one accessible platform. The website features dedicated Moon and Mars exploration sections, six documented mission artifacts, historical information, NASA source references, and an interactive quiz to help visitors understand the significance of these objects.

Through an engaging space-themed interface and interactive visual elements, we aim to make space history more accessible and interesting for students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

These objects may have been abandoned, but the knowledge, discoveries, and human achievements associated with them should never be forgotten. Our project transforms forgotten footprints of exploration into a digital space archive for future generations.
details: Our project is an interactive digital archive that explores human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars after space exploration missions. Space missions may end, but the objects and equipment they leave behind still hold important scientific, technological and historical value. However, their stories are not always easy for the public to discover. Our website aims to make this information accessible through an engaging digital experience. It presents the history and significance of abandoned space objects and helps visitors understand their connection to past and future space exploration. How it works Users can explore our website to learn about objects left behind during space missions, discover their stories and understand why they matter. The project focuses on presenting space exploration history in an interactive and visually engaging format. Benefits and intended impact - Preserves awareness of human space exploration history. - Makes information about lunar and Martian mission artifacts easier to explore. - Encourages interest in astronomy, science and space technology. - Highlights the scientific and historical value of objects that remain after missions. Technology used Our project is developed as a web-based experience. The technologies used in our implementation include React, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS and Three.js-based 3D graphics where implemented. Creativity and approach Instead of presenting the topic as an ordinary information page, we wanted to create an immersive digital archive. Our team focused on combining research, visual storytelling and interactive web design to make the history of abandoned space objects more engaging and memorable. Our goal is simple: to show that even when a space mission ends, its footprint should not be forgotten.
